finding.summary: Windows case-insensitive alias acceptance and case-sensitive copytree ignore can leave a destination symlink for copy2 to follow.
finding.source_gate: Path comparisons on Windows accept PYTHON3.EXE as python3.exe.
finding.sink: omit_launcher uses literal membership; shutil.copy2(...,follow_symlinks=False) does not refuse an existing destination link.
finding.minimal_fix: Refuse any existing destination, or create it exclusively with xb, before copying only the verified private interpreter; make alias omission case-consistent or reject other spelling.
finding.scope: Neutral two-file POSIX fixture simulates Windows directory spelling; actual Windows executable locking and damage are not claimed.

other_review_conclusions: Default no_links refusal remains unchanged except structured diagnostic.
Alias exception requires top-level path, symlink tag, exact SDK python.exe spelling and samefile ordinary target.
The approved alias is omitted before copytree and materialized from verified private python.exe on the expected lowercase path.
Source before/after include alias target and identity plus all logical entries.
Bootstrap opt-in is limited to automatically selected base bound to current executable; explicit source keeps old strict policy.
Workflow changes only add separate debug evidence and retain original candidate assets and time limits.
